messages.author: f769d7d2cfcf4edc
messages.subject: Monitor on one extracted chain
parts:
Hello yet again everyone,

My model is frequently multi-modal due purely to a label-switching problem.
E.g., running the model with 4 chains, 2:4 all converge to the same mode, but chain 1 converges to the same solution with reversed labels. That is, chains 2:4 may have alpha[1,1:2] as [1,2] and chain 1 as [2,1].
Thankfully, there is no within-chain label switching, so I can look at the posterior estimates for chains in the same modes:  monitor(extract(stanOut,pars='alpha',permuted=FALSE)[,2:4,])
That works great; however, I cannot do: monitor(extract(stanOut,pars='alpha',permuted=FALSE)[,1,]), because monitor() expects a 3D array, and [,1,] creates a 2D array.

Is there any way of using monitor (for the summary statistics) when extracting only one chain?

messages.author: f769d7d2cfcf4edc
messages.subject: Re: Monitor on one extracted chain
parts: Oh, a PS on this: Yes, I know I could just use apply() and compute the descriptives myself, but monitor() is just convenient, is all.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Monitor on one extracted chain
parts:
On Sunday, October 16, 2016 at 6:47:47 PM UTC-4, Stephen Martin wrote:
That works great; however, I cannot do: monitor(extract(stanOut,pars='alpha',permuted=FALSE)[,1,]), because monitor() expects a 3D array, and [,1,] creates a 2D array.
monitor(extract(stanOut,pars='alpha',permuted=FALSE)[,1,,drop = FALSE])
